Let \(a=BC\), \(b=AC\), and \(T=[ABC]\).

Since \(AD\) is the angle bisector,
\[
\frac{[ABD]}{[ADC]}=\frac{BD}{DC}=\frac{AB}{AC}=\frac7b.
\]
The parallel segment \(EF\) lies inside \(\triangle ADC\), so the three equal-area regions are \(\triangle ABD\), trapezoid \(ADFE\), and \(\triangle EFC\). Hence
\[
[ABD]=\frac T3,\qquad [ADC]=\frac{2T}{3}.
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{[ABD]}{[ADC]}=\frac{1}{2}=\frac7b,
\]
so
\[
b=14.
\]
Now \(BC=a\) must satisfy the triangle inequality:
\[
14-7 < a < 14+7 \implies 7<a<21.
\]
The integral values are
\[
8,9,\dots,20,
\]
which are \(13\) values.

\[
\boxed{13}
\]
